notes: Cutting out parts of a video (Subject Tracker 'Only the parts with subjects', Motion Trimmer, Trim Ends) works on more kinds of video. In a test on 100 security videos, 14 failed the quick cut and were re-encoded in full instead (slower, and bigger files), and 3 of those were refused altogether. Three causes, all fixed:

Videos that store B-frames: every copied stretch took 3 frames from after its end along. Now the copy stops at the last frame it can stop at cleanly, and the one or two frames after it are re-encoded.

Videos whose frame rate changes (10 frames a second in one stretch, 15 in the next): the re-encoded edges were spaced evenly, so a part could come out seconds too long. Every frame now keeps its own time.
Re-encoded edges of only one or two frames were read back half a frame short, so the next piece started too early. Each piece's length is now set exactly.
A re-encoded piece could leave out its own first frame and take one from after its end instead (its start time was rounded past the frame). It now starts at its first frame.
The check after a cut now also makes sure every frame is at its own time, and it no longer calls a correct B-frame video 0.13 s out of step.
